reference_drawer.description: Essential formulas for calculating the median of grouped data.

items.rule: First class whose cumulative frequency reaches or exceeds N/2.
items.example: For $N=30$, locate the first class with $cf\ge15$.
Here $cf$ is the cumulative frequency of the preceding class.
If cumulative totals are $5$ and $13$, the corresponding frequency is $8$.

items.rule: Convert discontinuous integer classes into continuous boundaries.

concepts.title: 1. Cumulative Frequency and Median Class
concepts.subtitle: Locate the central position
concepts.summary: Construct cumulative frequency by adding frequencies successively. The median class is the first class where cumulative frequency reaches or exceeds N/2.
concepts.trap: Using the median-class cumulative frequency instead of the preceding class cumulative frequency.

concepts.title: 2. Median Formula
concepts.subtitle: Use the preceding cumulative frequency
concepts.summary: After locating the median class, use its lower boundary, the preceding cumulative frequency, its frequency, class width, and N/2.
concepts.trap: Putting the median-class cumulative frequency in the numerator.

concepts.title: 3. Missing Frequencies
concepts.subtitle: Use N and median as independent conditions
concepts.summary: For two missing frequencies, the total-frequency condition gives one equation and the median condition gives a second equation. Solve them together.

points.text: Use the given median in the grouped-data formula for the second condition.

concepts.trap: Trying to find two unknown frequencies from only the total-frequency condition.

concepts.title: 4. Cumulative and Discontinuous Data
concepts.subtitle: Convert first, then calculate
concepts.summary: Recover ordinary frequencies from less-than or more-than cumulative totals using successive differences. Convert discontinuous integer limits using ±0.5 before applying the median formula.
concepts.trap: Using cumulative totals as ordinary frequencies or using unadjusted discontinuous limits.
